risks.name: Accidental Activation
risks.likelihood_rationale: Four mandatory gates all fail (0/4 PASS per S602 Trigger Registry). Seven prohibited activation paths documented (including stealth authoring, de facto operation, pilot/trial without gate satisfaction, single-lead activation, and Agent AA delegation). The S600 Charter §0 Standing Order explicitly states 'S600 is not an execution lane — it is a reserve charter.' Any agent attempting 600-series work without authorization would require circumventing DRIFT_001 (new SESSION6XX artifacts in reports/), DRIFT_004 (REVISION_HISTORY attribution to 600-series), T0 session startup checks (AGENTS.md §9), and the governance guard Rule 5 (30-item batch cap). The governance infrastructure makes accidental activation a multi-layer defense bypass — unlikely without deliberate circumvention.
risks.impact_rationale: If a future session inadvertently launched 600-series work, it would: (1) violate the S724 Executive Board's unanimous 26/26 deferral vote, (2) create a lane with documented negative ROI (Net -2.5 sessions per S602 revalidation), (3) consume 4 sessions of startup overhead for zero net benefit, (4) introduce ownership conflicts (C-001, C-002 unresolved, C-005 blocking) that would destabilize the portfolio, and (5) create governance precedent that reserve charters can be activated outside the defined gate structure.
mitigations: DRIFT_001 signal (CRITICAL — unauthorized 600-series artifacts detected at any cadence triggers HALT and governance audit)
DRIFT_004 signal (CRITICAL — REVISION_HISTORY entry attributing work to 600-series without Executive Board vote triggers revert and escalation)
S600 Charter §0 Standing Order — explicitly prohibits any 600-series activity outside authorized activation
S602 Trigger Registry prohibited activation paths 1-7 — single authoritative list of invalid activation attempts
T0 session startup check (AGENTS.md §9) — confirms S600 Charter hash unchanged and zero new 600-attributed artifacts every session
Governance guard Rule 5 (BLOCK — 30-item batch cap) — prevents bulk content operations under 600 authority without explicit BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker
risks.residual_rationale: The layered defense (DRIFT signals + T0 checks + Trigger Registry + Charter §0) makes accidental activation improbable. An agent would need to: write 600-attributed artifacts, evade DRIFT_001 detection, survive T0 hash verification, avoid triggering DRIFT_004 in REVISION_HISTORY, and circumvent the governance guard batch cap. This is a four-layer defense that would require deliberate circumvention, not accidental drift. The only material vulnerability is the 0/6 ownership acceptance state (GAP-3 PENDING) — the Governance Board, which would be the escalation recipient for DRIFT signals, has not formally accepted stewardship. Per the S726 dissenting note: 'if the governance actor itself fails to execute against a documented escalation,' the framework's enforcement is tested and found insufficient. This is a procedural vulnerability in the escalation chain, not a design vulnerability in the detection layer.
risks.assessment: Least concerning of the seven risks given current governance posture. The S602 Trigger Registry's 7 explicit prohibited paths eliminate ambiguity about what constitutes unauthorized activation. DRIFT_001 and DRIFT_004 provide immediate detection at any cadence. The S600 Charter §0 Standing Order is unambiguous. The residual LOW rating reflects the strength of the detection infrastructure, mitigated only by the GAP-3 ownership gap which weakens the escalation chain's reliability.

risks.name: Ownership Creep
risks.likelihood_rationale: The S600 Charter §2.1 authorizes broad-scope work labeled 'draft-preparation support,' 'modernization preparation,' and 'authoring support' — terms that naturally abut 800-series responsibilities. As the 800-series nears 100% Certification (~2,181 of 2,500 items = 87.2%), the remaining work shifts from certification (CAQS §1.6 audits) to post-certification modernization (DL-013 cleanup, DL-031 recalibration). A future session running 800-series modernization might naturally drift into 'preparing drafts for modernization' — which the charter defines as 600 work. The subjective boundary between 'preparation' (600 domain) and 'execution' (800 domain) is the vulnerability. The S725-S727 governance sessions themselves (read-only boundary audits, charter validation, monitoring frameworks) demonstrated that governance sessions can operate near the boundary without crossing it — but a content-modification session under 800 authority has a thinner buffer.
risks.impact_rationale: De facto activation without a vote undermines: (1) the S724 26/26 unanimous deferral, (2) the economic gate (Net -2.5 would be incurred without authorization), (3) the governance framework's credibility (if a lane can be activated by gradual scope expansion, the trigger registry and activation gates lose authority). The 800-series naturally owns modernization execution — any shift of modernization work into 600-labeled activity creates ownership ambiguity, duplicate effort, and governance conflict (C-001 unresolved).
mitigations: S601 boundary revalidation (Agent B, 95/100 integrity score) — confirmed boundaries are logically sound and procedurally enforced
S602 Ownership Conflict Review (Agent D, 5 conflicts classified) — C-001 (800 handoff) and C-002 (700 authority) classified as CARRY_FORWARD, explicitly requiring resolution during activation review
S725 Ownership Matrix Row 16 — reserves annual reactivation criteria review, establishing a formal check on scope drift
Monitoring Framework Deep Audit (every 20 sessions) — includes cross-series dependency impact assessment
DRIFT_002 signal (HIGH — any mandatory gate transitions FAIL→PASS) — would detect if ownership drift changed the activation calculus
S725-S727 governance sessions model the correct behavior: read-only boundary audits operating near the 600 boundary without crossing it
risks.residual_rationale: While the monitoring framework and boundary revalidation cadences provide periodic checks, the fundamental vulnerability is the subjective distinction between 'preparation' (600) and 'execution' (800) in the modernization context. The S600 Charter §2.2 explicitly prohibits modernization as 600 work, but a session characterizing modernization tasks as 'draft preparation' could exploit the semantic gap. The critical weakness is that GAP-3 remains PENDING — the Governance Board has not accepted stewardship of the 600 lane, meaning there is no accountable owner to detect or challenge creeping scope expansion. The Deep Audit every 20 sessions (~S620, est. August 2026) is the next formal check — a window of 17+ sessions where creep could occur without formal review. This risk is structurally similar to RISK_4 (Modernization Overlap) but distinct: RISK_2 is gradual scope expansion across sessions, while RISK_4 is a deliberate characterization of modernization as preparation in a single session.
risks.assessment: The most plausible path for involuntary 600 activation. The charter's broad authorization language ('authoring support,' 'modernization preparation') creates a semantic gray zone that 800-series agents operating post-certification could drift into. The S601/S602 boundary revalidations established clarity for the DEFERRED state, but the boundary will be tested when 800 reaches post-certification modernization. The 0/6 ownership acceptance state means no steward is watching for this specifically. Residual MEDIUM reflects the combination of: well-defined but subjectively-interpretable boundaries + ownership vacuum + 17-session monitoring gap between Deep Audits.

risks.name: Analytics Duplication
risks.likelihood_rationale: The S600 Charter §3.1 is unambiguous: '600 MAY NOT produce independent analytics that compete with or duplicate 300-series outputs.' The 300-series owns all analytics models (DQS, EQS, BQS, ExQS, UIQS, Risk Register, Forecast Engine, Bottleneck Analysis). No 600-series agent is active, and no session has produced analytics under 600 attribution. The 300-series itself is approaching S310 closeout — analytics production is winding down, not ramping up, reducing the surface area for duplication. A session spinning up independent analytics would need to: (1) not know the 600 charter exists, (2) not know 300 owns analytics, (3) claim the work as 600-series, and (4) evade DRIFT_001 detection. This is a four-factor conjunction — low probability.
risks.impact_rationale: If duplicated analytics were produced, they would: (1) violate the single-source-of-truth principle (S600 Charter §6), (2) create conflicting quality scores or throughput metrics that mislead governance decisions, (3) waste session resources producing redundant outputs, and (4) create confusion about which analytics authority is canonical for governance purposes.
mitigations: S600 Charter §3.1 explicit prohibition: '600 MAY NOT produce independent analytics that compete with or duplicate 300-series outputs'
S600 Charter §2.2: 'Analytics — Owned By: 300-series' with explicit list of prohibited 600 activity
DRIFT_001 signal (CRITICAL) — any new 600-attributed artifact triggers HALT and governance audit
300-series is the established sole authority for all analytics — no other lane claims analytics production
risks.residual_rationale: The charter prohibition is absolute and unambiguous. The 300-series analytics monopoly is well-established. No past session has attempted analytics under non-300 attribution. The DRIFT signals provide immediate detection. This is the most straightforward risk to mitigate — the charter says 'no,' and the monitoring framework says 'we'll check.' No subjective boundary interpretation is required.
risks.assessment: Lowest-concern risk. The prohibition is categorical, the detection is straightforward, and there is no operational incentive for a session to produce 600-attributed analytics. The 300-series closure (S310 pending) further reduces the analytics production surface. This risk exists as a theoretical possibility but has zero evidence of materialization and strong structural prevention.

risks.name: Modernization Overlap
risks.likelihood_rationale: This is the most operationally proximate risk. The 800-series manages both certification (active) and post-certification modernization (approaching). The S600 Charter §2.1 authorizes 'modernization preparation — preparing content batches, organizing draft queues, and staging materials for 800-series certification passes.' The S600 Charter §2.2 prohibits modernization as 600 work: 'Modernization execution — Owned By: 800-series.' The boundary between 'preparation' and 'execution' is thin and context-dependent. As the 800-series nears 100% Certification (2,181 of 2,500 = 87.2%), the remaining 319 items plus post-certification DL-013/DL-031 workloads will create pressure to characterize modernization tasks as 'preparation' to claim 600 authority without the activation vote. The S724 Agent V criterion AV_4 explicitly identifies this scenario ('post-certification modernization phase where batch DL-013/DL-031 ops become new bottleneck') as a reactivation evaluation trigger — recognizing the boundary's vulnerability.
risks.impact_rationale: If modernization work is executed under 600 authority without activation: (1) the S724 deferral is subverted — a lane producing negative ROI would be activated de facto, (2) the Governance Board's authority is bypassed — the activation vote requirement is moot if work simply gets relabeled, (3) C-001 (800 handoff friction) and C-002 (700 authority drift) become live operational conflicts without resolution, (4) the 800-series loses control of modernization quality standards, and (5) the governance framework's credibility is fundamentally damaged — if 'preparation' can mean 'execution,' the charter's prohibitions are unenforceable.
mitigations: S600 Charter §2.2 explicit prohibition: 'Modernization execution — Owned By: 800-series. 600 MAY NOT make certification decisions, change question_state, promote content to production, verify or modify answer keys, approve content for learner delivery.'

S724 Agent V criterion AV_4 explicitly identifies this boundary: 'Post-certification modernization phase where batch DL-013/DL-031 ops become new bottleneck' is a trigger for re-evaluation, not for de facto activation
S602 Trigger Registry TRIGGER_BACKLOG and TRIGGER_DEDICATED_LANE require 300-series evidence before reactivation is worth evaluating
DRIFT_001 and DRIFT_004 detect unauthorized 600-attributed artifacts
Charter §3.3: '600 MAY NOT make any certification decision' — modernization operations that touch question_state, answer keys, or production deployment are unambiguously prohibited
risks.residual_rationale: The charter draws a clear line in principle: preparation (research, staging, drafting) is 600; execution (certification decisions, state transitions, production deployment) is 800. But modernization work like DL-013 distractor authoring sits in the gray zone — it is content writing (could be 'preparation') that directly modifies pack files (could be 'execution'). A session might argue: 'We're just authoring ExplanationWrong fields as draft content — the 800-series will review and certify' — framing DL-013 cleanup as preparation rather than execution. The residual MEDIUM rating reflects: (1) the charter's prohibition is clear but the semantic boundary is subjective, (2) 800-series approaching 100% creates operational pressure on this boundary, (3) GAP-3 (0/6 ownership acceptances) means no steward is monitoring the boundary specifically, and (4) the S724 AV_4 criterion's existence proves the framework anticipated this risk — but anticipation is not prevention. The four-layer defense (charter prohibition + DRIFT signals + trigger registry + charter §3.3) provides strong but imperfect protection.
risks.assessment: The highest-impact risk because it could subvert the entire deferral framework through semantic reinterpretation rather than overt violation. The S600 Charter correctly separates 'preparation' from 'execution,' but the operational reality of modernization work blurs this distinction. The residual MEDIUM risk is driven by: (1) the approaching 800-series endpoint will test this boundary in practice, (2) the GAP-3 ownership vacuum means no accountable steward exists to adjudicate boundary disputes, and (3) the subjective nature of 'preparation' vs. 'execution' for content-authoring tasks makes DRIFT signal detection less reliable than for overt violations like creating new charter documents or analytics artifacts.

risks.name: Governance Debt Accumulation
risks.likelihood_rationale: GAP-3 (Governance Board acceptance of S725 Row 16) has been PENDING since S725 (2026-07-26) and has passed three deadlines: S726 T0, S727 T0, and now S603 without resolution. The evidence is undisputed: S726 Ownership Acceptance Registry records 0/6 acceptances, all 6 past deadline. S725 COND-04 required ownership acceptance before S726 T0 — FAILED. S726 COND-S726-001 escalated to P0 IMMEDIATE with S727 T0 deadline — FAILED. ESC-S726-001 triggered CRITICAL escalation with the finding that 'the governance actor itself fails to execute against a documented escalation.' The S726 dissenting note warned: 'if ownership acceptances remain at 0/6 past the escalated deadline, the determination will shift to ADDITIONAL ENFORCEMENT REQUIRED — because the framework's own enforcement mechanism will have been tested and found insufficient.' This prediction has materialized. The governance debt is not just PENDING — it is compounding. Each session that passes without resolution adds another data point confirming the framework's enforcement weakness.
risks.impact_rationale: The orphaned lane creates cascading vulnerabilities: (1) no accountable owner to detect unauthorized 600 activity (weakens RISK_1 mitigation), (2) no steward to adjudicate ownership creep boundary disputes (weakens RISK_2 mitigation), (3) no entity authorized to hold the GATE_BOARD activation vote (weakens the entire gate structure), (4) the governance framework's Principle 2 (acceptance requirement) is demonstrably inoperative — damaging the framework's normative force for all 6 gaps, not just GAP-3, and (5) the S726 Board's conditional HARDENED status (with dissenting note) is itself contingent on ownership resolution — unresolved GAP-3 arguably downgrades the framework from HARDENED to DESIGN-ONLY. The impact is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the dormancy controls (DRIFT signals, T0 checks, charter prohibitions) operate independently of ownership acceptance — the lane remains dormant and governed even without an accepted steward.
mitigations: COND-S726-001: P0 IMMEDIATE — Governance Board must resolve 0/6 ownership acceptance state with S727 T0 deadline (PASSED — now carries forward to S603+)
ESC-S726-001: CRITICAL escalation — requires Governance Auditor to initiate acceptance protocol at S727 T0, notify all 6 assigned owners, prepare succession activation for non-responsive owners
Stewardship Framework §5.3 succession plan: 'Governance Auditor assumes unaccepted responsibilities after 3-session escalation window' (S728 T0 = activation trigger)
Annual stewardship review (2027-07-26) — formal governance check that will flag unresolved GAP-3 as a charter amendment trigger
Monitoring Framework Deep Audit (S620, est. August 2026) — includes stewardship acceptance status check
risks.residual_rationale: The framework has a documented resolution path (succession plan §5.3 activates at S728 T0) — the Governance Auditor will automatically assume orphaned responsibilities if owners remain unresponsive. This is a hard backstop. The residual MEDIUM (not LOW) reflects: (1) the succession plan hasn't been tested — the Governance Auditor assuming 6 additional responsibilities (across 100/300/500/600/700/800 lanes) is an untested reallocation of governance capacity, (2) the procedural history (3 missed deadlines) indicates non-performance risk even for the succession plan, and (3) the governance debt has already accumulated — the S725 COND-04, S726 COND-S726-001, and ESC-S726-001 deadlines have all passed, creating a pattern of escalation without execution that weakens future enforcement credibility. However, the dormancy controls (DRIFT signals, T0 checks, charter) operate correctly regardless of ownership status — the lane remains governed even if no one has formally accepted the keys.
risks.assessment: The most likely risk — it is not a prediction, it is an observation. GAP-3 has accumulated across 3 governance sessions with zero progress. The escalation machinery (COND, ESC) has produced documentation but not execution. The succession plan (§5.3) provides a self-correcting mechanism at S728 T0, which limits the worst case. But the pattern of documented escalation without resolution is itself a governance risk: each missed deadline erodes the framework's credibility as a binding governance mechanism. This risk is LIKELY to continue (no evidence of imminent resolution), but the IMPACT ceiling is capped by the succession plan backstop and the operational independence of the dormancy controls from ownership acceptance.

risks.name: Charter Rot
risks.likelihood_rationale: The S600 Charter v1.0 was created 2026-07-26 and references a specific portfolio configuration: 300-series active (pre-S310 closeout), 700-series in maintenance mode, 800-series at 87.2% Certified, and the 300→600→800 pipeline as the intended operating model. Several portfolio changes are already in motion: (1) 300-series S310 closeout will transition 300 to CLOSED, removing one leg of the 300→600→800 pipeline, (2) 800-series certification approaching 100% will shift the lane's purpose from certification to modernization, (3) S728 Deep Audit may introduce new governance standards that alter ownership boundaries, (4) the SESSION_STATUS handoff document (AGENTS.md §9 primary reference) is already stale (2,031 vs. 2,181 certified). The charter's assumptions about portfolio structure could become outdated within the next 5-10 sessions as 300 closes and 800 transitions.
risks.impact_rationale: An outdated charter would mislead future activation evaluations. If the 300-series closes, the 300→600→800 pipeline no longer exists — but activation gates might still be evaluated against the charter's original pipeline model. The charter's economic assumptions (4-session startup, 3-session savings) were calculated against a specific portfolio size and 800 workload — if the 800 workload shrinks below the charter's assumptions, the economic gate would understate the true startup cost per remaining item. The charter's ownership boundaries (§3) reference active 300/700/800 lanes — if 300 closes and 800 transitions, the boundaries need recalibration. An incorrect evaluation could lead to: (1) false activation — gates appear satisfied under outdated assumptions, or (2) false permanent deferral — gates appear to fail under outdated assumptions when they should pass under current conditions.
mitigations: Annual stewardship review (2027-07-26) — formal charter relevance assessment at Lane 600 level
Monitoring Framework Deep Audit (every 20 sessions) — includes 'Is the S600 Charter still the correct operating model?' as a specific check
S600 Charter §9 amendment process — requires Executive Board vote (300+700+800 leads) for any amendment, preventing unilateral charter changes
DRIFT_002 signal (HIGH) — any mandatory gate transition triggers Governance Board re-evaluation, which inherently validates charter assumptions
DRIFT_006 signal (MEDIUM) — 800-series certification completion triggers AV_4 re-evaluation
Charter versioning (§9.2) and status tracking (§9.4) provide explicit amendment history, preventing silent drift
risks.residual_rationale: The charter has multiple scheduled reviews (annual + Deep Audit every 20 sessions + DRIFT-triggered reviews) that provide layered protection against staleness. The §9 amendment process requires Executive Board consensus — no single lane can unilaterally update the charter. The charter's status tracking fields (§9.4) create a formal record of when it was last reviewed, making staleness visible. The residual LOW rating reflects: (1) the multiple review cadences provide frequent checks, (2) the amendment process prevents unauthorized updates, (3) portfolio changes (300 closeout, 800 transition) are high-visibility events that would naturally trigger charter review, and (4) unlike RISK_5 (where the enforcement mechanism is demonstrably failing), the charter review mechanism has not yet been tested. The risk is that the review mechanism could also fail to execute — the same 0/6 ownership acceptance pattern — but the review cadence is annual and the first review (2027-07-26) is far enough out that portfolio changes will be well-established by then.
risks.assessment: A real but well-mitigated risk. The charter was written for a specific portfolio state that is already evolving (300 closeout imminent, 800 approaching 100%). The multiple review cadences and formal amendment process provide structural protection. The primary vulnerability is execution risk — if the annual review is missed due to the same governance execution failures documented in RISK_5, the charter could stale without detection. However, the charter's assumptions are unlikely to become critically wrong within a 12-month window given the relatively stable portfolio structure (same 5 packs, same 2,500 items, same CAQS standard).

risks.name: Monitoring Fatigue
risks.likelihood_rationale: Multiple signals indicate monitoring fatigue is already present: (1) SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24.md is stale — reports 2,031 Certified (vs. 2,181 actual, a 150-item undercount), 67 phantom DL-008 items (vs. 0 actual), and DL-016 severity LOW (vs. HIGH actual). AGENTS.md §9 directs every new session to read this file first — meaning every session since S802 has been operating on incorrect governance data. S726 COND-S726-007 required this to be superseded before S727 T0 — it was not. (2) 0/6 ownership acceptances despite 3 passed deadlines — the governance execution function itself is not performing. (3) The T0 session startup check (AGENTS.md §9) adds ~30 seconds per session — minimal but requiring consistent execution. (4) The Rapid Pulse cadence (every 5 sessions at S605) is approaching with no evidence of preparation. (5) S726 ESC-S726-002 rated this as HIGH severity and required resolution before S727 T0 — it was not resolved. The governance execution layer (not the design layer) is showing strain.
risks.impact_rationale: If monitoring stops: (1) DRIFT signals would not be evaluated — unauthorized 600 activity could go undetected for sessions, (2) the S600 Charter hash could change without detection (DRIFT_003 bypassed), (3) activation gates could silently flip without triggering the Governance Board review required by DRIFT_002, (4) the dormant lane could become genuinely ungoverned — the Charter and Monitoring Framework exist on paper but have no operational enforcement, and (5) the distinction between DORMANT AND GOVERNED (current state) and DORMANT AND UNMONITORED (deteriorated state) could blur without anyone noticing. The impact ceiling is that all other risk mitigations fail simultaneously — monitoring fatigue is a systemic risk that amplifies all other risks.
mitigations: AGENTS.md §9 Session Startup Protocol — mandates T0 monitoring as a per-session requirement: 'read SESSION_STATUS for open risks,' 'verify question_state Certified count via direct raw-file grep,' 'cross-check open remediation proposals against current state'
S602 Monitoring Framework — defines 4 explicit cadences with specific checks, actions, and escalation paths (T0 per session, Rapid Pulse at 5, Deep Audit at 20, Annual)
Review ownership assigned to Governance Auditor (700-series Maintenance Mode) — named responsible party with defined escalation path
Governance Auditor's maintenance mode responsibilities (S723 Maintenance Framework) include monitoring trigger thresholds and cadenced checks

DRIFT signals are automated detection mechanisms — they fire based on artifact presence, not human vigilance. DRIFT_001 (new artifacts) and DRIFT_003 (charter tampering) trigger on file changes regardless of whether anyone was watching
risks.residual_rationale: The framework design is sound: automated DRIFT signals provide passive detection even without active monitoring; the T0 startup protocol is embedded in AGENTS.md (the first file every session reads); the Governance Auditor is a named role with defined responsibilities. However, execution evidence is poor: SESSION_STATUS staleness (150-item certified undercount, 67 phantom DL-008), missed COND-S726-007 deadline, 3 missed ownership acceptance deadlines. The residual MEDIUM reflects the gap between design (excellent) and execution (deteriorating). The automated DRIFT signals provide a floor — unauthorized 600 artifacts would still be detected by file-change-based signals even if no human auditor was actively monitoring. But the nuanced signals (DRIFT_002 gate transition, DRIFT_006 800 completion) require active evaluation — they do not fire automatically on file changes. These could be missed if the monitoring cadences slip. The 17-session gap between S602 and the next Deep Audit (S620) is the longest monitoring gap in the framework — fatigue risk is highest in this window.
risks.assessment: The systemic risk — monitoring fatigue doesn't create new vulnerabilities, it removes the detection layer for all other risks. The current evidence (SESSION_STATUS staleness, missed deadlines, 0/6 acceptances) indicates the governance execution layer is already degraded. The automated DRIFT signals provide a safety net but only for artifact-level violations (new files, charter tampering, REVISION_HISTORY entries). The more nuanced monitoring (gate transitions, boundary creep, charter relevance) requires active governance that is currently not performing. The residual MEDIUM reflects: good design + poor execution = elevated but not critical risk. The S603 session itself (this risk assessment) is an example of governance function operating correctly — suggesting the capability exists even if consistency is not yet demonstrated.

risk_heatmap.critical_rationale: No risk achieves CRITICAL severity. All risks have documented mitigations in place, and the dormant lane imposes zero operational burden on active lanes. The absence of CRITICAL risks reflects the governance framework's maturity: S600-S602 established a comprehensive dormancy governance model before the lane entered its dormant period.

high_risks.name: Governance Debt Accumulation
high_risks.rationale: HIGH likelihood (actively materialized — GAP-3 PENDING across 3 sessions with 3 missed deadlines) + MEDIUM impact (orphaned lane, but dormancy controls operate independently of ownership) = HIGH overall. The 0/6 ownership acceptance state is the single most significant governance vulnerability in the portfolio.

high_risks.name: Modernization Overlap
high_risks.rationale: MEDIUM likelihood (800 approaching 100% creates operational pressure on the preparation/execution boundary) + HIGH impact (would subvert deferral, bypass Governance Board vote authority) = HIGH overall. This is the risk most likely to materialize as the 800-series enters post-certification operations.

medium_risks.name: Ownership Creep
medium_risks.rationale: MEDIUM likelihood (subjective boundary between 600 preparation and 800 execution + 17-session Deep Audit gap) + MEDIUM impact (de facto activation without vote, ownership ambiguity) = MEDIUM overall.

medium_risks.name: Charter Rot
medium_risks.rationale: MEDIUM likelihood (portfolio evolving — 300 closing, 800 transitioning) + MEDIUM impact (misleading activation evaluations) = MEDIUM overall. Well-mitigated by multiple review cadences.

medium_risks.name: Monitoring Fatigue
medium_risks.rationale: MEDIUM likelihood (already evidenced by SESSION_STATUS staleness, missed deadlines) + MEDIUM impact (detection layer degradation amplifies all other risks) = MEDIUM overall. Automated DRIFT signals provide a floor.

low_risks.name: Accidental Activation
low_risks.rationale: LOW likelihood (4 mandatory gates all FAIL + 7 prohibited paths + 4-layer defense) + HIGH impact = LOW residual. Multi-layer detection infrastructure makes accidental activation improbable.

low_risks.name: Analytics Duplication
low_risks.rationale: LOW likelihood (absolute charter prohibition + no operational incentive + 300 monopoly) + MEDIUM impact = LOW overall. The most straightforward risk to mitigate.

overall_risk_rationale: The 600-series dormant lane is well-governed at the design layer (Charter, Trigger Registry, Monitoring Framework, DRIFT signals, ownership matrix) but under-executed at the activation layer (0/6 ownership acceptances, stale SESSION_STATUS, 3 missed deadlines). The governance framework's design is strong enough to prevent CRITICAL failures — no risk achieves CRITICAL severity, and all risks have documented mitigations. However, the execution gap (GAP-3 PENDING, monitoring fatigue evidence) creates systemic vulnerability: the same governance execution function that failed to accept ownership and update the handoff document is the function responsible for executing the monitoring cadences that protect against Risks 1-4 and 6-7. The rating is ELEVATED (not ACCEPTABLE) because: (1) RISK_5 (Governance Debt) is not a risk — it is an ongoing incident that has survived 3 sessions without resolution, (2) RISK_4 (Modernization Overlap) has a subjective boundary that will be tested as 800 approaches 100% with no accountable steward to adjudicate, and (3) the monitoring fatigue evidence (stale handoff, missed deadlines) suggests the governance execution layer is deteriorating. The rating is ELEVATED (not UNACCEPTABLE) because: (1) the dormant lane imposes zero operational burden and has zero active agents, (2) the automated DRIFT signals provide passive detection independent of active monitoring, (3) the Stewardship Framework §5.3 succession plan activates at S728 T0 — a hard self-correcting backstop, (4) the S603 session itself (this risk assessment, deferred-state audit, prior S601/S602 governance work) demonstrates governance function operating correctly when activated, and (5) zero content impact across all 600-series sessions (S600-S603: 0 pack-file modifications, 0 question_state changes, 0 certification decisions).

The 0/6 acceptance state has persisted through 3 deadlines. Per S726 Board Decision dissenting note: the framework's own enforcement mechanism has been tested and found insufficient. Either: (a) the Governance Board explicitly accepts S725 Row 16 stewardship, or (b) the succession plan (§5.3) is formally acknowledged as the resolution path with S728 T0 as the activation trigger.
recommended_additional_controls.rationale: This is the root vulnerability that amplifies all other risks. Without ownership acceptance, no entity is accountable for the 600 lane. Every other mitigation depends on a steward who can detect, escalate, and resolve issues.

Update AGENTS.md §9 to reference the current handoff document.

Include concrete examples: e.g., 'authoring ExplanationWrong text for a pack file' = execution (800 domain); 'compiling a COSO misconception catalog for Section E items' = preparation (600 domain). This specification should be incorporated into the S600 Charter as §2.1a.

Executing it successfully establishes a track record of governance execution, directly countering the monitoring fatigue risk. A missed Rapid Pulse would confirm the fatigue pattern and justify escalating the overall risk rating to UNACCEPTABLE.

recommended_additional_controls.description: After 300-series S310 closeout, reassess the S600 Charter's pipeline model. If the 300-series transitions to CLOSED, the 300→600→800 pipeline reference in §1.1 becomes outdated. The charter should either: (a) remove the 300-series from the pipeline model and reflect the new 600→800 direct pipeline, or (b) add a note documenting that the 300-series role in the pipeline has transitioned to 700-series consumption (GAP-2).
recommended_additional_controls.rationale: The charter's pipeline model is its strategic rationale. If the model no longer reflects the portfolio, future activation evaluations will be flawed. This is a scheduled amendment, not an emergency — the Deep Audit at S620 is the correct cadence.

recommended_additional_controls.description: Add a 'DRIFT_007' signal: 'Any session produces a SESSION_STATUS or REVISION_HISTORY entry with a certified count that differs from the governance baseline by >10 items without explanation.' This closes the detection gap that allowed the SESSION_STATUS to stale with a 150-item undercount without triggering an alert.
recommended_additional_controls.rationale: The current DRIFT signals detect artifact creation and charter tampering but not data staleness in governance documents. A certified-count drift signal would have caught the SESSION_STATUS undercount before it became the default handoff document for multiple sessions.

conclusion: The 600-series dormant lane is governed at the design layer but under-executed at the activation layer — zero critical risks exist, but the 0/6 ownership acceptance state and approaching 800-series post-certification boundary create ELEVATED residual risk requiring the Governance Board to either accept stewardship or formally activate the succession plan before the S620 Deep Audit.
